name: Ignorance (avidyā)
description: In Advaita the root cause of bondage: the superimposition of self and not-self, or the positive power that veils the self and projects the world; removed only by knowledge.

name: Ignorance, desire and action (avidyā-kāma-karma)
description: The chain of bondage in Śaṅkara's commentaries: ignorance gives rise to desire, desire to action, action to embodiment and suffering; cut at the root by knowledge.

name: The three defects of the mind: impurity, distraction, veiling
description: Impurity (mala) removed by selfless action, distraction (vikṣepa) removed by meditation/worship (upāsanā), and veiling (āvaraṇa) removed by knowledge — the rationale of the ordered sections of the Veda and Gītā.

name: The four obstacles to nirvikalpa samādhi
description: Dullness (laya), distraction (vikṣepa), latent attachment (kaṣāya) and relishing (rasāsvāda).
antidotes: do not relish bliss; be unattached by discernment

name: Dullness (laya)
description: The mind's lapsing into sleep for want of support; the mind should be roused (GK 3.44).

name: Distraction (vikṣepa)
description: The mind's running to external things; it should be calmed again (GK 3.44).

name: Latent attachment (kaṣāya)
description: The mind stiffened by latent impressions of attachment, neither distracted nor absorbed; it is to be recognized.

name: Relishing the bliss (rasāsvāda)
description: Enjoying the bliss of absorption (savikalpa) and resting there, which prevents going beyond; one should be unattached through discernment (GK 3.45).

name: The obstacles to samādhi in the Aparokṣānubhūti
description: Lack of inquiry, laziness, desire for enjoyment, dullness, darkness, distraction, relishing and blankness, to be gradually abandoned by the knower of Brahman.

name: Doubt about the means of knowledge (pramāṇa-saṃśaya)
description: Doubt whether the Upaniṣads really teach the non-dual Brahman; removed by hearing.

name: Doubt about the object (prameya-saṃśaya, asambhāvanā)
description: Doubt whether the self can possibly be Brahman; removed by reflection.

name: Contrary habitual notion (viparīta-bhāvanā)
description: The deep-rooted habit of taking oneself to be body and mind, persisting after understanding; removed by contemplation.

name: The three tendencies (vāsanā-traya)
description: Tendencies toward the world (reputation), toward scriptural learning (pedantry) and toward the body, which prevent right knowledge — 'iron fetters'.

name: Obstructions to knowledge (pratibandha)
description: Knowledge arises in this life only if no obstruction is present (BS 3.4.51): present obstructions (attachment to objects, dull intellect, perverse reasoning, obstinate misconception), past tendencies, and future karma requiring further births.

name: The knot of the heart (hṛdaya-granthi)
description: The ego-knot tying consciousness to the insentient body-mind; cut when the self is seen (MU 2.2.8).

name: Identification of self with body (dehātma-buddhi)
description: Taking the body as 'I', the grossest form of superimposition, basis of caste, stage and all empirical claims.
